explain.say: Here is a magic little word: yet. "I cannot do it" becomes "I cannot do it yet." That tiny word means you are still on your way. This way of thinking is called a growth mindset. Can you add yet to something you find hard?

faq.a: A growth mindset is believing that you can get better at things with practice, good ways of learning and help. It is the difference between "I cannot do it" and "I cannot do it yet".
asks: What does the power of yet mean?

faq.q: Why does practice make things easier?
faq.a: Every time you practise, the connections between the brain cells you use get stronger and faster. After lots of practice, the skill becomes almost automatic, like riding a bike.
asks: How does practice change my brain?

faq.q: Why do I sometimes stop improving?
faq.a: Learning often goes flat for a while, which is called a plateau. It is normal. Try a new way of practising, ask for tips, or rest, and the next jump usually comes.
asks: Why am I stuck and not getting better?

faq.q: Can anyone have a growth mindset?
faq.a: Yes. A growth mindset is a way of thinking, and you can learn it, just like any skill. Everyone has some fixed-mindset moments too.

faq.q: Does a growth mindset mean I can do anything?
faq.a: Not instantly or perfectly. It means you can improve with effort, good strategies and help from others. Everyone grows at their own speed.
asks: Can I be good at everything if I try?

facts: Psychologist Carol Dweck of Stanford University made the idea of a growth mindset famous in her 2006 book Mindset.
A 2000 study found that London taxi drivers, who learn the city's thousands of streets, had a larger hippocampus, a brain area used for memory and maps.
